response.title: which off grid inverters are approved for a permit
response.answer:
In the United States, off-grid solar inverters can be approved for building and electrical permits, but approval depends on the inverter's safety certifications and the requirements of your local building department (AHJ — Authority Having Jurisdiction).

For a residential off-grid solar installation, the most important certifications are:

Certification

	

Why it matters




UL 1741

	

Primary safety standard for solar inverters and power conversion equipment




UL 1741 SB

	

Advanced grid-interconnection requirements; generally relevant to grid-connected or hybrid systems




UL 9540

	

May be required for a complete battery energy storage system




IEEE 1547

	

Relevant when connecting to the utility grid




UL 1973

	

Safety certification for stationary batteries

A true off-grid system that never connects to the utility generally does not need IEEE 1547 or UL 1741 SB grid-interconnection functionality. However, it still needs appropriately listed equipment and a code-compliant installation.

Specific off-grid inverter models to consider

EG4 6000XP

UL 1741 certified

6 kW, 120/240V split-phase, 48V battery system.

A strong candidate for a permit application. EG4 publishes an Intertek cETLus UL 1741 certificate for this model. 
EG4 Electronics
+1

View certification

Sol-Ark 15K-2P

15 kW, 120/240V split-phase, 48V battery system.

A higher-capacity hybrid option supporting off-grid operation and grid interconnection, with UL 1741 SB certification reported. Verify the exact model listing and battery combination before submitting plans. 
Live Off The Grid
+1

For California permits

California's electrical safety requirements are not the same as the California Energy Commission's inverter equipment list. An inverter can be UL 1741 certified without necessarily appearing on the CEC list, and some local authorities impose additional requirements.

You can check the California Energy Commission equipment lists.

For example, Sunnyvale's published residential PV checklist specifically requires inverters to be UL 1741 listed. 
Sunnyvale
 Other jurisdictions can require load calculations, battery capacity documentation, disconnects, and additional design details.

markup:
In the United States, **off-grid solar inverters can be approved for building and electrical permits**, but approval depends on the inverter's safety certifications and the requirements of your local building department (AHJ — Authority Having Jurisdiction).

For a residential off-grid solar installation, the most important certifications are:

| Certification | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **UL 1741** | Primary safety standard for solar inverters and power conversion equipment |
| **UL 1741 SB** | Advanced grid-interconnection requirements; generally relevant to grid-connected or hybrid systems |
| **UL 9540** | May be required for a complete battery energy storage system |
| **IEEE 1547** | Relevant when connecting to the utility grid |
| **UL 1973** | Safety certification for stationary batteries |

A true off-grid system that never connects to the utility generally does **not** need IEEE 1547 or UL 1741 SB grid-interconnection functionality. However, it still needs appropriately listed equipment and a code-compliant installation.

  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="EG4 6000XP off grid solar inverter product white cabinet" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="116px" shop_eligible={true}/>

      **<Entity category="product" value="EG4 6000XP"/>**

      <badge color="success">UL 1741 certified</badge>

      6 kW, 120/240V split-phase, 48V battery system.

      A strong candidate for a permit application. EG4 publishes an Intertek cETLus UL 1741 certificate for this model. <Cite refs={["turn801125search25","turn801125search6"]}/>

      <Link url="https://eg4electronics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/EG4-6000XP-UL1741-Certificate-of-Compliance.pdf" title="View certification"/>
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>

    <box flex="1" gap={1}>

      15 kW, 120/240V split-phase, 48V battery system.

      A higher-capacity hybrid option supporting off-grid operation and grid interconnection, with UL 1741 SB certification reported. Verify the exact model listing and battery combination before submitting plans. <Cite refs={["turn801125search7","turn801125search4"]}/>
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## For California permits

California's electrical safety requirements are not the same as the California Energy Commission's inverter equipment list. An inverter can be UL 1741 certified without necessarily appearing on the CEC list, and some local authorities impose additional requirements.

You can check the <Link url="https://www.energy.ca.gov/programs-and-topics/programs/solar-equipment-lists" title="California Energy Commission equipment lists"/>.

For example, Sunnyvale's published residential PV checklist specifically requires inverters to be UL 1741 listed. <Cite ref="turn801125search24"/> Other jurisdictions can require load calculations, battery capacity documentation, disconnects, and additional design details. <Cite ref="turn801125search3"/>

## Two questions so I can narrow this down

{@body const [system,setSystem] = DIL.useState("offgrid")}
<box gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Find specific off-grid inverter models eligible for electrical permits in "+location+". System type: "+(system==="offgrid"?"completely off-grid with no utility connection":"hybrid with utility grid connection")+". Include certification evidence and permit considerations.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Where are you applying for the permit?</label>
      <input value={location} onChange={setLocation} placeholder="City, state or country"/>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What type of system?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={system} onChange={setSystem}>
        <radio value="offgrid">Completely off-grid, no utility connection</radio>
        <radio value="hybrid">Hybrid, connected to the utility grid</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button submit block>Find permit-eligible inverters <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those details, I can narrow the list to specific inverter models and the certifications your permitting authority is likely to require.
